context.description: Stage 5 finished, all tasks done and api-tests green. This scenario built/changed OrderService.createOrder and the order-confirmation view. PriceHelper.round is a shared helper this scenario did NOT touch. ReportService.exportMonthly is unrelated code this scenario did NOT touch.
context.note: Anomaly routing (steps 4-5): a confirmed anomaly that belongs to THIS scenario → recommend reject (workflow loop-back), not captured; anything else → self-report kind:issue, then fix-now (trigger define-task) or later (parked).

evals.title: Agent-detected concern, out-of-scenario → confirmed → issue
evals.prompt: At the concerns step, while reviewing you notice PriceHelper.round (a shared helper this scenario did not touch) rounds half-down, which looks wrong for money totals. Handle it.
expectations: Raises it to the user as a concern — does NOT itself decide it is a bug
On the user confirming it is real, routes it as out-of-scenario → triggers self-report with kind: issue (places includes PriceHelper.round)
Does NOT reject the scenario over it (it is not part of this scenario)
Does NOT author or run a fix itself

evals.title: Agent-detected concern dismissed → dropped
evals.prompt: You raised the PriceHelper.round concern. The user says: 'no, half-down is intentional for our accounting — not a bug.' Proceed.
expectations: Nothing is recorded — no kind: issue entry is created and tech-debt.js is not written
The scenario is not affected
The agent accepts the user's judgment — the user decides right/wrong, not the agent

evals.title: User-raised anomaly that belongs to THIS scenario → reject loop-back, not an issue
evals.prompt: At the 'anything wrong?' step, the user says: 'the order confirmation we just built shows the wrong currency symbol.' Handle it.
expectations: Recognizes it belongs to this scenario (part of what was just built)
Recommends the user reject, so workflow loops it back to Stage 1 as a fast feedback loop (the existing additive loop-back)
Does NOT capture it as a kind: issue in tech-debt.js
Does NOT trigger define-task

evals.title: User-raised out-of-scenario anomaly, fix now → issue + define-task
evals.prompt: At the 'anything wrong?' step, the user says: 'unrelated to this feature, but ReportService.exportMonthly still imports the legacy mongo client — dead dependency. Let's get it fixed now.' Handle it.
expectations: Routes it as out-of-scenario → triggers self-report with kind: issue (places includes ReportService.exportMonthly)
Because the user chose fix-now → triggers define-task on that entry's id
Does NOT reject the scenario — its accept/reject is unaffected
Does not itself design or author the fix — define-task does

evals.title: User-raised out-of-scenario anomaly, later → issue only, parked
evals.prompt: Same dead-dependency anomaly as before, but the user says: 'just log it for later, don't fix it now.' Handle it.
expectations: self-report writes the kind: issue entry to tech-debt.js
define-task is NOT triggered — the entry is parked and surfaces in feed-back.html for a later run
The scenario's accept/reject is unaffected

evals.title: Closing feedback is a separate question from anomalies
evals.prompt: At the retrospective closing-feedback step, the user gives process feedback: 'the integration tests were slow this round.'
expectations: The closing-feedback question is asked separately from the anomaly steps (it is not merged with 'anything wrong?')
Process feedback is sent to self-report as a new occurrence — NOT as a kind: issue
It is not run through the Anomaly routing (no scenario-vs-issue split, no fix-now/later)
